question: Patients on isoniazid which vitamin deficiency is more likely to be seen.
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Isoniazid" -> "interferes with pyridoxine metabolism" -> "Vitamin B6 deficiency" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Isoniazid" -> "increased excretion of pyridoxine" -> "Vitamin B6 deficiency" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Isoniazid" -> "possible interference with vitamin absorption" -> "Vitamin B6 deficiency" -> 85%
analysis: Isoniazid is an antibiotic commonly used in the treatment of tuberculosis. It is well-documented in medical literature that isoniazid can lead to a deficiency in Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine). This occurs because isoniazid acts as a pyridoxine antagonist, interfering with its metabolism and increasing its excretion. This interaction can lead to symptoms of Vitamin B6 deficiency, such as peripheral neuropathy. To prevent this, patients on isoniazid are often co-prescribed Vitamin B6 supplements. Other vitamins like B9, B12, and B3 are not typically affected by isoniazid in the same manner. Therefore, the most likely vitamin deficiency in patients taking isoniazid is Vitamin B6.
